title: Past Tenses: Choosing the Right One
grammarTitle: The Four Past Tenses — When to Use Each
grammarNote: В английском языке четыре основных прошедших времени. На уровне A2 вы изучили их базовое использование. На B1 важно понимать тонкие различия — когда одно предпочтительнее другого, и как они взаимодействуют в одном тексте или разговоре.

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple
grammarTable.example: "She arrived at 9." / "He studied all night." — single completed event.

grammarTable.subject: Past Continuous
grammarTable.example: "She was studying when he called." — ongoing at that moment.

grammarTable.subject: Past Perfect
grammarTable.example: "She had studied all night before the exam." — earlier than another past event.

grammarTable.subject: Past Perfect Continuous
grammarTable.example: "She had been studying for hours when he arrived." — ongoing duration before past event.

grammarExtra.title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous: completed vs ongoing

rows.form: Past Simple = completed event at a point
rows.example: "She called at 8." (one moment) / "He studied economics." (completed course of action)
"She was working when he called." (working = ongoing background; called = interruption)
"While she was reading, he was cooking." (simultaneous background activities)
"She read for an hour, then cooked dinner." (sequence, not background)

grammarExtra.title: Past Perfect: establishing sequence in narrative

rows.form: Use PP to clarify which event came FIRST
rows.example: "When I arrived, she had already left." (left = earlier; arrived = later) ✅

rows.form: No PP needed for simple sequence
rows.example: "She finished eating, then left." (clear order with "then" — no PP needed) ✅
"She realised she had made a mistake." / "He noticed he had forgotten his keys." ✅
"She said she had already submitted the form." (said = PS; submitted = PP) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Past Perfect Continuous: duration before a past moment

rows.example: "He had been waiting for two hours when she arrived." (two hours of waiting before arrival)

rows.form: Explains visible result at past moment
rows.example: "Her eyes were red because she had been crying." (crying explains the red eyes)
"She had written the essay." (completed) vs "She had been writing the essay." (process)
"He had been studying for three hours." / "She had been waiting since 9 a.m." ✅

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Common B1 mistakes with past tenses

rows.example: ✅ "When I arrived, she had already left." — use PP for the earlier action.

rows.form: ✗ "I was studying when I passed the exam."
rows.example: ✅ "I was studying when I took the exam." (Continuous = ongoing, not completed result)

rows.form: ✗ "She had been writing the essay." (= completed)
rows.example: ✅ "She had written the essay." — PP Simple for completion. Continuous = process.

rows.form: ✗ "He had been gone to the shop."
rows.example: ✅ "He had gone to the shop." — "gone" cannot be continuous! Only dynamic verbs. ✅

grammarTip:
Четыре прошедших времени — выбор:

Past Simple → ЗАВЕРШЁННОЕ действие в прошлом:
"She arrived at 9." / "He studied for years."

Past Continuous → ФОНОВОЕ/ПРОДОЛЖАВШЕЕСЯ действие:
"She was studying when he called."

Past Perfect → БОЛЕЕ РАННЕЕ прошлое:
"By the time I arrived, she had already left."

Past Perfect Continuous → ПРОДОЛЖИТЕЛЬНОСТЬ до прошлого момента:
"She had been working for hours when he arrived."

💡 Ключевые вопросы:
→ Было ли действие завершено? → Past Simple
→ Было ли оно фоном/прерванным? → Past Continuous
→ Произошло ли оно раньше другого прошлого? → Past Perfect
→ Продолжалось ли оно до прошлого момента? → PP Continuous

exercises.instruction: Choose the most natural past tense.
exercises.text: When Amir ___ to WKU, he ___ never live away from home.
exercises.hint: "When Amir CAME to WKU, he HAD never lived away from home." PS for main event + PP for state up to that point. ✅

exercises.instruction: Which tense shows a background activity?
exercises.text: "She ___ her notes when the phone rang."
exercises.hint: Past Continuous = background, ongoing action that was interrupted. "She WAS REVIEWING when the phone rang." ✅

exercises.text: "By the time the lecture started, she ___ (read) the whole chapter."
exercises.hint: "By the time + PS → PP." "By the time it started, she HAD READ the chapter." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which sentence shows duration before a past moment?
exercises.text: Choose the sentence using Past Perfect Continuous correctly.
opts: "She had been waiting for an hour when he arrived."
exercises.correct: "She had been waiting for an hour when he arrived."
exercises.hint: "had been waiting" = PP Continuous → duration (one hour) before a past moment (his arrival). ✅

exercises.text: "___ he was writing, she ___ to music."
exercises.hint: Two simultaneous background actions = both Past Continuous. "While he WAS WRITING, she WAS LISTENING." ✅
PP Continuous explains a visible state at a past moment. "He HAD BEEN CRYING." (duration of crying → explains red eyes) ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ her notes, ___ a coffee, and ___ her laptop."
opts: was reviewing / was making / was opening
had reviewed / had made / had opened
exercises.hint: Simple sequence of completed events = all Past Simple. No need for Continuous or Perfect here. ✅

exercises.instruction: PP Simple vs PP Continuous. Choose the PROCESS.
exercises.text: "By 3 a.m., he ___ for five hours." (emphasise the ongoing process)
exercises.hint: PP Continuous = emphasises the process/duration. "He HAD BEEN STUDYING for five hours." ✅ PP Simple would emphasise completion.

exercises.instruction: Reported speech — choose the tense shift.
exercises.hint: Reporting past speech shifts tenses back. "has submitted" → "HAD submitted." ✅ Present Perfect → Past Perfect in reported speech.

exercises.text: "She reached for her card and realised she ___ (leave) it at home."
exercises.hint: "realised" = PS; the leaving happened BEFORE the realisation → Past Perfect. "She HAD LEFT it at home." ✅

exercises.text: "When I got to the bus stop, the bus ___."
exercises.hint: "had just left" = PP, the bus left BEFORE I arrived. Just = very recently. ✅

exercises.text: "She had been gone to the library." — What is wrong?
opts: "had been gone" is wrong — "go" cannot be used in continuous → "had gone"
exercises.correct: "had been gone" is wrong — "go" cannot be used in continuous → "had gone"
exercises.hint: Stative or resultative verbs ("be gone") don't use continuous. ✅ "She HAD GONE to the library." ✅

opts: A background or ongoing action at a past moment
A duration before a past event
questions.correct: A background or ongoing action at a past moment
questions.hint: Past Continuous = what was going on in the background, or ongoing at a specific past time. ✅

questions.text: "She had already left when I arrived." — "had left" is used because:
opts: Her leaving happened BEFORE my arrival
questions.correct: Her leaving happened BEFORE my arrival
questions.hint: Past Perfect = earlier past. Her leaving came BEFORE my arrival. ✅

questions.text: "He had been waiting for two hours." — What does this emphasise?
opts: The duration of waiting before a past moment
questions.correct: The duration of waiting before a past moment
questions.hint: PP Continuous = emphasises how long something was going on before a past reference point. ✅

questions.text: "When she woke up, she realised she ___ (miss) her alarm."
questions.hint: "realised" = PS; missing happened BEFORE the realisation → Past Perfect. "She HAD MISSED her alarm." ✅

questions.text: "While he was cooking, she was reading." — Both Continuous because:
opts: They are two background simultaneous activities
Both were completed at the same time
questions.correct: They are two background simultaneous activities
questions.hint: Two simultaneous ongoing background actions → both Past Continuous. ✅

questions.text: "She read the chapter, then closed her notebook." — Why Past Simple both?
opts: It's a simple completed sequence — no complex overlap
questions.correct: It's a simple completed sequence — no complex overlap
questions.hint: Simple sequential events with "then" = Past Simple both times. No need for Continuous or Perfect. ✅

questions.text: "She had written the essay." vs "She had been writing the essay." — difference:
opts: "had written" is for irregular verbs only
questions.hint: PP Simple = completion/result. PP Continuous = ongoing process/duration. ✅

questions.text: "Her eyes were red because she ___ (cry) for an hour."
questions.hint: PP Continuous = duration that explains a past visible state. "She HAD BEEN CRYING for an hour." ✅

questions.text: "She said she HAD SUBMITTED the form." — "had submitted" instead of "has submitted" because:
opts: In reported speech, PS→PP and PP stays PP; Present Perfect→Past Perfect
questions.correct: In reported speech, PS→PP and PP stays PP; Present Perfect→Past Perfect
questions.hint: In reported past speech, all tenses shift back. Present Perfect → Past Perfect. ✅

opts: "She had been gone to the library."
questions.hint: "While she WAS READING (Continuous), he CALLED (PS — interruption)." ✅ All others have errors.

questions.text: "He had been studying for 5 hours." — With which time expression is this most natural?
opts: "He had been studying for 5 hours when she arrived."
questions.correct: "He had been studying for 5 hours when she arrived."
questions.hint: "had been studying FOR 5 hours WHEN she arrived." — PP Continuous + duration + past reference point. ✅

questions.text: Choose the sentence with the correct use of all four past tenses.
opts: "She had been working when she was realising she had forgot her keys."
"She was working in the office. By 3pm, she had already finished what she had been doing since morning."
"She has been working and left after realised she was forgetting her keys."
"She worked while she had been leaving."
questions.correct: "She was working in the office. By 3pm, she had already finished what she had been doing since morning."
questions.hint: Was working (background PC) → had finished (PP completion) → had been doing (PP Continuous duration). ✅
